introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three (booklets GCE/P/2021/0595/3/C/Grp 1, Grp 2 and Grp 3). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only (the printed paper does not say how the groups are allotted).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the picture 'CornerShop' found on the desktop, Group Two Task II) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

incertitudes: Le PDF (18 pages, scan sans couche texte) contient TROIS versions du meme sujet pratique : « Group One » (pages 1 a 6, livret GCE/P/2021/0595/3/C/Grp 1), « Group Two » (pages 7 a 12, Grp 2) et « Group Three » (pages 13 a 18, Grp 3), chacune avec Task I (traitement de texte, 20 points), Task II (tableur, 20 points) et Task III (programme C ou Pascal, 10 points). Page de garde verifiee : ORDINARY LEVEL, COMPUTER SCIENCE, 0595, Paper 3, juin 2021, 2h30. Transcrites en neuf fichiers : numero_exercice G1-T1, G1-T2, G1-T3, G2-T1, ..., G3-T3 ; groupes ["GROUP 1"], ["GROUP 2"] ou ["GROUP 3"]. Le sujet n'impose pas expressement de ne traiter qu'une version (le candidat ne passe en pratique qu'un groupe) : non exprimable, regles_choix reste vide. De meme, a la Task III le sujet dit « Select any one of them » (programme C ou Pascal) : non exprimable.

Les filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo, les cadres d'en-tete (numero de centre, nom du candidat, « For examiners' use only »), les lignes a completer, les textes fantomes du verso (le papier est translucide) et les artefacts de scanner sont ignores. Le fichier-image « CornerShop » (Group Two, Task II) et les fichiers du bureau ne figurent pas dans le PDF.

Aucun logiciel (traitement de texte, tableur) n'a ete execute : les menus et les etapes sont donnes de memoire (Office recent) et ne sont pas testes. Les formules de tableur ont ete traduites en Python et executees sur les donnees du sujet (totaux, moyennes, calcul des frais, tri). Aucun compilateur C ou Pascal n'est disponible : les programmes du sujet n'ont pas ete compiles, leur logique a ete verifiee par une simulation Python fidele (division entiere et reste, memes entrees, memes sorties) dont les resultats sont recopies dans les corriges.
Aucun corrige officiel n'existe : les reponses sont redigees. Les repartitions de points dans les corriges (« marking idea ») sont indicatives ; les points imprimes du sujet ne sont jamais modifies.

Pascal : les entiers du programme sont declares « integer ». Sur un compilateur a entiers de 16 bits (maximum 32767, cas d'anciens Turbo Pascal ou du mode par defaut de certains compilateurs) une entree comme 45678 (Group One) provoque un depassement ; sur un compilateur a entiers de 32 bits (cas usuel, et int en C) le resultat est celui donne. Le corrige indique la sortie attendue sur une machine a entiers de 32 bits. En Pascal ISO la largeur d'affichage par defaut d'un entier est definie par l'implementation : le corrige suppose l'affichage sans blancs de tete (cas usuel).

Task 2, Group Two : les points imprimes (2 + 2 + 2 + 5 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 20) correspondent a l'en-tete ; la question 4 (save and print) n'a pas de points. La question 1 (lettres a, b, c : 2 points chacune) est transcrite en UNE seule question numero 1 (6 points) ; les sous-questions 2a a 2e (5, 2, 2, 2, 2 points) et 3 (1 point) sont des questions distinctes (numero 2a ... 2e, 3). Les marques de droite, decalees par le texte fantome du verso, sont affectees ligne a ligne (2d : 2 ; 2e : 2).

Figure 2 : le scan est sur papier translucide (texte fantome du verso visible) ; la figure est REDESSINEE (memes colonnes A a H, memes lignes 1 a 14, memes entrees et valeurs) ; l'image du logo « CornerShop » (ligne 2) n'etant pas dans le PDF, elle est remplacee par un encadre « [image CornerShop] ». La cellule du mot « Totals » est lue comme D14 (l'etiquette est a droite de la colonne Qty Sold) : les totaux sont donc attendus en E14:H14.

Calculs : Total Sales = Unit Cost x Qty Sold ; Gross Profit = 20 % du total ; Tax = 5 % du gross profit (le sujet dit « the gross profit is taxed at 5% ») ; Net Profit = gross profit - tax. Tri : « descending order of net profit » ; Bread et Eggs ont le meme net profit (950), leur ordre relatif n'est pas determine.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Launch the spreadsheet software on your computer, and create a workbook called Task2.

a. Increase the height of Row 1 to 30, merge cells in the range A1:H1 and type the text centered as shown with font Bookman Old Style font size 24 and coloured blue.  *[2 marks]*
b. Increase the height of Row 2 to 116; merge cells in the range A2:H2 and insert the image called *CornerShop* found on the desktop. Resize the image to an appropriate size.  *[2 marks]*
c. Increase the height of Row 3 to 20, merge cells in the range A3:H3 and type the text centered as shown with font Bookman Old Style font size 14 and coloured blue.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Start the spreadsheet (for example *Microsoft Excel*), open a new workbook and save it at once under the name **Task2**.

**a.** Right-click the header of row 1 > **Row Height** > **30**. Select **A1:H1** and click **Merge & Center** (*Home* > *Alignment*). Type **Corner Shop Groceries** in the merged cell. With the cell selected: font **Bookman Old Style**, size **24**, *Font Color* > **Blue**. (2 marks)

**b.** Row 2: **Row Height** > **116**. Select **A2:H2** > **Merge & Center**. With the merged cell selected, *Insert* > **Pictures** > browse to the desktop and choose the image **CornerShop**. Resize it by dragging a corner handle (keep the proportions) so that it fits inside the merged cell A2:H2. (2 marks)

**c.** Row 3: **Row Height** > **20**. Select **A3:H3** > **Merge & Center**. Type **Main Street Avenue Douala**; font **Bookman Old Style**, size **14**, colour **blue**. (2 marks)

Note: the picture file is supplied on the day; it is not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown: Type the text in Columns A, B, C, D as shown; **maintain the formatting**.  *[5 marks]*
Type a formula in cell E5 to calculate the total sales of Oil and copy the formula down to other items.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total sales = unit cost x quantity sold. Click **E5** and type `=C5*D5`, press *Enter* (7200). Select E5, drag the fill handle (small square at the bottom right corner) down to **E13** (or double-click it). Each row adapts the references (`=C6*D6`, ... `=C13*D13`).

Values (Python simulation): Oil 7200, Bread 5000, Butter 3750, Cheese 1000, Sugar 8000, Eggs 5000, Tea 1200, Lemon Juice 2000, Milk 10800.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the Gross profit is 20% of total sales, type a formula in cell F5 to calculate the Gross Profit of Oil and copy the formula down to other items.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click **F5** and type `=E5*20%` (or `=E5*0.2`), press *Enter* (1440). Copy the formula down to **F13** with the fill handle.

Values: Oil 1440, Bread 1000, Butter 750, Cheese 200, Sugar 1600, Eggs 1000, Tea 240, Lemon Juice 400, Milk 2160.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the gross profit is taxed at 5%, calculate the tax amounts for each item and hence then net profit using spreadsheet formulas.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tax = 5% of the gross profit: in **G5** type `=F5*5%`, copy down to G13. Net profit = gross profit minus tax: in **H5** type `=F5-G5`, copy down to H13.

Values (Python simulation):

| Item | Gross profit | Tax (5%) | Net profit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oil | 1440 | 72 | 1368 |
| Bread | 1000 | 50 | 950 |
| Butter | 750 | 37.5 | 712.5 |
| Cheese | 200 | 10 | 190 |
| Sugar | 1600 | 80 | 1520 |
| Eggs | 1000 | 50 | 950 |
| Tea | 240 | 12 | 228 |
| Lemon Juice | 400 | 20 | 380 |
| Milk | 2160 | 108 | 2052 |

(Equivalent: `=F5*0.95` for the net profit.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Use spreadsheet formulas to calculate the indicated totals.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The word *Totals* is on row 14 (D14): the totals are required in the columns that were calculated, E to H. Click **E14** and type `=SUM(E5:E13)`, then copy it to F14, G14 and H14 (or type `=SUM(F5:F13)`, `=SUM(G5:G13)`, `=SUM(H5:H13)`).

Values (Python simulation): **E14 = 43950**, **F14 = 8790**, **G14 = 439.5**, **H14 = 8350.5**. (Check: 8790 - 439.5 = 8350.5.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Sort the items in descending order of net profit.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the table of items **A5:H13** (the data rows only: not the headings, not the *Totals* row). *Data* tab > **Sort**, choose **Sort by: Net Profit** (column H), **Order: Largest to Smallest** (or select a cell of column H and click *Sort Largest to Smallest*). The whole rows move together, so each item keeps its own figures.

Order obtained (Python simulation): Milk 2052, Sugar 1520, Oil 1368, Bread 950, Eggs 950 (equal net profit: Bread and Eggs tie), Butter 712.5, Lemon Juice 380, Tea 228, Cheese 190.

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task 2 in your working directory and print a copy.
questions.corrige_markdown: *File* > **Save As**, working directory (the *Candidate folder*), name **Task 2**, then *File* > **Print** and print one copy. No mark is printed for this step.
